text:
Alex: Heads up — after today's merge (runtimelib: kernel-switcher change), we're seeing a noticeable tail CPU spike on the KV-heavy workloads in the staged rollout.  p95 CPU increased ~30% on a 20% traffic cohort.
PerfBot: CI perf check failed for commit abc123 (regression detected). Perf failure: p95_cpu_tokens/sec drop > 20%. See: https://ci.redwood/telem/abc123
Maya: I rolled up the PR that touched batching heuristics + kernel selector: it swapped the default kernel hint for long-context models. The change was intended to improve throughput for seq>2048 but might hurt short-seq KV paths.
Jun: Uploading quick flamegraph sample from the canary host:
``` 
# flamegraph top
kernel_select (40%)\nkv_lookup (25%)\nattention_kernel_v2 (20%)\nother (15%)
```
Jun: The stack shows increased time in kernel_select leading to more context rebuilds which amplify KV miss cost. Suspect heuristics path is misclassifying short sequences and forcing an expensive kernel.
Liam: Can we pause the staged rollout? Current rollout is at 20% prod. I propose reducing to 5% or pausing until we bisect. If it affects p95 it's a rollout blocker.
Nina: Agreed. I'll trigger a staged-rollout pause in console and pin the traffic to the previous model variant. Action: pause->done (console transaction id tx_9922).
Arun: For bisect, suggest: `git bisect start --bad abc123 --good def456 && git bisect run ./scripts/perf_check.sh`. I can run a targeted bisect across the kernel switch commits tomorrow.
Maya: Also found a related unit: batching heuristics were flipped to always prefer "dense batching" when estimated batch_size > 8. That interacts poorly with KV cached requests which have bursty small requests. Patch in PR: https://reviews/redwood/4521
Alex: We need a short-term mitigation: 1) pause rollout (done), 2) revert kernel hint in runtime for canary pool (create revert PR), 3) run bisect + perf CI. Who takes revert?
Liam: I'll open the revert PR now and include an A/B gating flag: runtime.kernel_selector.use_legacy_hint=false -> true for canary. I'll target minimal revert.
PerfBot: Notifying monitoring: p95 CPU alert throttled at 25% over baseline — alert created INC-2025-77
Jun: Quick perf test on canary host with revert applied locally shows p95 back to baseline. Patch looks like the culprit.
Nina: I'll watch the dashboards and keep the rollback paused until we confirm revert in nightly CI. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/p/kv-metrics (p95 cpu, kv-miss-rate, batching-size-dist)
Arun: After revert merge, propose an automated guard: rollout should auto-pause if p95 increases >15% or kv-miss-rate increases >10% for 5 consecutive minutes in canary cohort. We should encode that as a policy in the rollout manager.
Maya: Agree. Also add a pre-merge CI perf test that runs a small synthetic KV workload to catch this class of regression. It can be an opt-in long test on PRs touching batching/kernel logic.
Alex: Action items:
- Liam: open revert PR and link to this thread.
- Jun + Maya: run bisect and confirm root commit; attach flamegraphs.
- Nina: monitor dashboards and confirm when safe to resume.
- Arun: draft rollout guard policy (thresholds + time window) and add to rollout manager.
Liam: Revert PR opened: https://reviews/redwood/4527 — tagging @oncall for fast merge if CI passes.
PerfBot: CI for revert PR 4527 shows perf pass on the KV synthetic (p95 within 3% of baseline).
Alex: Good. Once revert merges we'll promote to canary at 5% and watch for 30 minutes before resuming larger rollout. If any alert triggers, auto-pause should hold it.
Maya: We should also add a regression note in the release notes and mention the new guardrails.
Jun: I'll post flamegraphs and a short postmortem draft after the bisect finishes.
Nina: I'll close the incident once metrics are stable for 2 hours after revert.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Quick wins: revert merged -> monitor -> add guard. Longer term: refine kernel selection heuristics to respect KV-burst patterns and update CI to include KV synthetic.
Arun: I'll start the PR for the rollout guard policy today, ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:
